In what year was Magnesium discovered?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12.
Adenosine: Pfizer. Adenosine (symbol A) is an organic compound that occurs widely in nature in the form of diverse derivatives.
Which country is HAL Tejas from?
HAL Tejas: India. The aircraft made its first flight in 2001 and entered into service with the IAF in 2015.
Who is credited with discovering Grus?
Grus (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Grus (or colloquially) is a constellation in the southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Reynolds number?
Reynolds number: Sir George Stokes, 1st Baronet. At low Reynolds numbers, flows tend to be dominated by laminar (sheet-like) flow, while at high Reynolds numbers, flows tend to be turbulent.
Who is credited with discovering Ceres?
Ceres (dwarf planet): Giuseppe Piazzi. Ceres is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
This localized collection of pus builds up within body tissue, usually from bacterial infection, causing redness, pain, warmth, and swelling. What is it?
Abscess is a collection of pus that has built up within the tissue of the body, usually caused by bacterial infection.
First described by Othniel C. Marsh in 1877, this late Jurassic theropod's name means 'different lizard,' a nod to its unusually lightweight vertebrae — what dinosaur is it?
Allosaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived 155 to 143 million years ago during the late Jurassic period (latest Oxfordian to latest Tithonian ages).

Named in 1835 from the Greek for 'flower' and 'dark blue,' these pH-shifting pigments paint blueberries, black rice, and some autumn leaves anything from red to purple to nearly black — what are they?

Anthocyanin (from Ancient Greek (nthos) 'flower' and / (kuneos/kuanos) 'dark blue'), also called anthocyans, are water-soluble vacuolar pigments that, depending on their pH, may appear red, pink, purple, blue, or black.
First described in 1740, this flowering-plant family rivals only the orchid family in sheer number of species, with over 32,000 recognized today — what family is it?
Asteraceae is a large family of flowering plants that consists of over 32,000 known species in over 1,900 genera within the order Asterales.

This fluid-dynamics rule holds that a fluid's pressure drops as its speed increases; the Swiss physicist credited with it published the idea in 1738, though Leonhard Euler derived the actual equation — what's it called?
Bernoulli's principle is a key concept in fluid dynamics that relates pressure, speed and height.
This incurable, always-fatal disease of cattle causes abnormal behavior and trouble walking, with symptoms that may take four to five years to appear after infection — what is this disorder called?
Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), commonly known as mad cow disease, is an incurable and always fatal neurodegenerative disease of cattle.

One species in this genus of flowering shrubs, native to southern China and Indochina, has its leaves processed into the world's tea, while thousands of ornamental cultivars exist for the garden. Name the genus?
Camellia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Theaceae.
Taken by mouth with effects lasting about a day, this second-generation antihistamine treats hay fever, hives, and dermatitis with less drowsiness than older allergy medications — what is it?
Cetirizine is a second-generation peripherally selective antihistamine used to treat allergic rhinitis (hay fever), dermatitis, urticaria (hives), and runny nose.
Its Latin genus name literally means three-leaf, and this herbaceous legume, native to Europe, now grows worldwide in around 300 species — what plant is it?
Clover are plants of the genus Trifolium (from Latin tres 'three' and folium 'leaf').

This cosmopolitan bird family includes crows, ravens, magpies, and jays, and its roughly 135 species are known for remarkable intelligence, including self-awareness demonstrated in mirror tests — what's the family?
Corvidae is a cosmopolitan family of oscine passerine birds that contains the crows, ravens, rooks, magpies, jackdaws, jays, treepies, choughs, and nutcrackers.

First patented in Germany in 1920, then independently synthesized by an American chemist in 1932 and marketed in German-speaking Europe as Permonid for its fast onset and short duration, what is this semi-synthetic opioid?
Desomorphine (or in some formulations known as Krokodil) is a semi-synthetic opioid commercialized by Roche, with powerful, fast-acting effects, such as sedation and analgesia.
Along with the platypus, this quill-covered Australian and New Guinean mammal is one of only two living egg-laying mammal groups, and its young are adorably called puggles — what is it?
Echidna are quill-covered monotremes (egg-laying mammals) belonging to the family Tachyglossidae, living in Australia and New Guinea.
This taxonomic family groups hedgehogs of Eurasia and Africa together with the furrier moonrats of Southeast Asia, and takes its name from the Latin for 'hedgehog' — what family is it?
Erinaceidae (from Latin erinaceus, "hedgehog") is a family in the order Eulipotyphla, consisting of the hedgehogs and moonrats.
This field of study, related to economics and business administration, is typically divided into personal, corporate, and public branches. What field is it?
Finance refers to monetary resources as well as the discipline that studies such resources, with related concepts such as money, currency, assets and liabilities.
Testimony at Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán's 2018 trial revealed suitcases stuffed with $3 million in bribes paid to this former Mexican security chief — who is he?
Genaro García Luna (born 10 July 1968) is a Mexican former government official and convicted drug trafficker.
This Italian-American motorsport boss ran a Formula One team for seven years before becoming CEO and owner of a MotoGP outfit — who is he?
Guenther Steiner (born 7 April 1965) is an Italian and American motorsport engineer and former team manager.
This seasonal state of low body temperature, slow breathing, and reduced metabolism helps some animals pass through winter months — what is it?
Hibernation is a state of minimal activity and metabolic reduction entered by some animal species.
First appearing in the fossil record in Egypt some 37 million years ago, this order of small African herbivores once rivaled odd-toed ungulates in size and diversity — which order?
Hyracoidea is a taxonomic order of mammals.

This English independent scientist invented the electron capture detector, was first to spot CFCs spread through the atmosphere, and proposed that the Earth behaves as one self-regulating system. Who was he?
James Lovelock (26 July 1919 - 26 July 2022) was an English independent scientist, environmentalist and futurist.
This Soviet-designed naval helicopter has spawned variants for assault transport, export, and civilian use, and still flies today from Russia to India -- which aircraft?

Kamov Ka-27 (NATO reporting name 'Helix') is a military helicopter developed for the Soviet Navy, and as of 2024 is in service in various countries including Russia, Ukraine, Vietnam, China, South Korea, and India.

A hybrid of the citron and the bitter orange believed to have originated in northeastern India around the 1st millennium BC, this small evergreen citrus tree bears a tart yellow fruit used worldwide — name the fruit?
Lemon (Citrus limon) is a species of small evergreen tree in the Citrus genus of the flowering plant family Rutaceae.
Dubbed the 'Queen of QVC' for her long-running shopping show and holding over 120 patents, this American entrepreneur is also an investor on the reality series Shark Tank — who is she?
Lori Greiner is an American television personality and entrepreneur.

This Milanese thinker was the first woman to write a mathematics handbook and the first appointed a mathematics professor — though she spent her final decades on theology and serving the poor. Who was she?
Maria Gaetana Agnesi (16 May 1718 - 9 January 1799) was a Milanese mathematician, philosopher, theologian, and humanitarian.

Named from Greek words meaning 'small head,' this congenital condition involves a smaller-than-normal head and can affect brain development, intellectual ability, and motor function — which disorder is it?
Microcephaly (from Neo-Latin microcephalia, from Ancient Greek mikrs "small" and kephal "head") is a medical condition involving a smaller-than-normal head.
Named for the strong odor males emit during rut to attract mates, this thick-coated Arctic hoofed mammal is called 'the bearded one' in Inuktitut — what's the species?
Muskox (Ovibos moschatus) is a hoofed mammal of the family Bovidae.
First isolated by Scottish physician Daniel Rutherford, which group-15 nonmetal with atomic number 7 is the most abundant species in Earth's atmosphere?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
The heaviest living bird, this flightless African species can sprint at 70 km/h and lays the largest eggs of any land animal on Earth — what bird is it?

A Chinese singer famous for annual appearances on a widely watched Lunar New Year television gala, she has served as her country's First Lady since 2012 as the wife of its paramount leader — who is she?

Peng Liyuan (pinyin: Png Lyun; born 20 November 1962) is a Chinese singer who has served as the First Lady of China since 2012, as the wife of Xi Jinping, the General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and paramount leader of China.
The sole genus in its plant subfamily, this evergreen conifer bears needle-like leaves in bunches of two to five and carries its seeds on woody cones — name the tree?
Pine is any conifer in the genus Pinus of the family Pinaceae.

This oral glucocorticoid medication suppresses the immune system and reduces inflammation in conditions like asthma and COPD, though long-term use risks side effects such as cataracts and bone loss — what's the drug called?
Prednisone is a glucocorticoid medication mostly used to suppress the immune system and decrease inflammation in conditions such as asthma, COPD, and rheumatologic diseases.
Element 88 on the periodic table, this silvery-white alkaline earth metal turns black when exposed to air and glows via radioluminescence as it radioactively decays — which element?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.

Usually hidden below the soil surface but sometimes growing aerial or aerating instead, these plant organs anchor a plant while drawing in the water and nutrients it needs to grow taller and faster — name them?
Root are the organs of a plant that are modified to provide anchorage for the plant and take in water and nutrients into the plant body, which allows plants to grow taller and faster.

Native to the North Pacific coasts, this marine mammal is the heaviest member of the weasel family yet one of the smallest marine mammals, insulated by the densest fur coat in the animal kingdom — what is it?
Sea otter (Enhydra lutris) is a marine mammal native to the coasts of the northern and eastern North Pacific Ocean.
Commonly but inaccurately nicknamed for a big cat it wasn't closely related to, this extinct genus of saber-toothed predator roamed the Americas until as recently as 8,200 years ago — which genus?
Smilodon is a genus of extinct felids. It is one of the best-known saber-toothed predators and prehistoric mammals.

Starting with fever and flu-like symptoms before the skin blisters and peels into painful raw patches, this severe drug-triggered skin reaction sits on the same disease spectrum as toxic epidermal necrolysis, only less severe — which condition?
Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS) is a type of severe skin reaction.

Tucked beneath the lateral fissure of the brain and named for its position near the head's temples, this region handles language comprehension, memory, and emotion — which part of the cerebral cortex?
Temporal lobe is one of the four major lobes of the cerebral cortex in the brain of mammals.
These brightly colored Neotropical birds are known for their oversized, vividly patterned bills, and their chicks hatch completely naked with no down feathers at all — what bird is it?
Toucan are Neotropical birds in the family Ramphastidae.
This member of the herpesvirus family causes chickenpox in children and, upon reactivation later in life, shingles in adults — what is it called?
Varicella zoster virus (VZV), also known as human herpesvirus 3 (HHV-3, HHV3), is one of nine known herpes viruses that can infect humans.
This broad category of limbless, tube-bodied animals ranges from microscopic creatures to a marine species measured at nearly 58 meters long — the longest animal on Earth — what are they called?
Worm are many different distantly related bilateral animals that typically have a long cylindrical tube-like body, no limbs, and usually no eyes.
This mucolytic drug is the go-to antidote for acetaminophen overdose, working by boosting glutathione to neutralize the drug's toxic byproducts — what is it?
Acetylcysteine: Medication used to treat overdose of paracetamol.
Twice President of the Swiss Confederation, this Social Democratic politician left the Federal Council in 2023 to become Secretary General of the Council of Europe — who is he?
Alain Berset: Swiss Federal Councillor from 2012 to 2023.
Nicknamed the boto for its rosy pink hue (especially in males), this South American toothed whale is the largest species of its kind found in a freshwater habitat — what is it?
Amazon river dolphin: Species of toothed whale. The position of the Araguaian river dolphin (I. araguaiaensis) within the clade is still unclear.
This American anthropologist studied women's weaving and blacksmithing work in Indonesia and later designed microcredit programs to fight rural poverty — who was she?
This pigmented ring of skin around the nipple contains sebaceous glands as well as the openings of the milk ducts — what's it called?
Areola: Pigmented area on the breast around the nipple.
The famous AL 288-1 skeleton nicknamed 'Lucy,' unearthed in Ethiopia's Afar region, belongs to which extinct East African hominin species that lived roughly 3.9 to 2.9 million years ago?
Australopithecus afarensis: Extinct hominid from the Pliocene of East Africa.
Sharing its engine, transmission, and rotor system with the Huey utility helicopter, this rapidly-developed attack chopper became America's dedicated gunship escort in the Vietnam War — what is it?
Bell AH-1 Cobra: Family of attack helicopters.

A French child prodigy who wrote a treatise on conic sections at 16, then built one of the first mechanical calculators and traded letters with Fermat that helped birth probability theory — who was he?
Created in 1993 by Swiss student Urban Müller, this esoteric programming language uses just eight simple commands and is often cited as a 'Turing tarpit' — what is it called?
Brainfuck: Esoteric, minimalist programming language. While Brainfuck is fully Turing-complete, it is not intended for practical use but to challenge and amuse programmers.
Discovered in 1817 simultaneously by two German chemists as an impurity in zinc carbonate, this soft silvery-white metal shares chemical traits with zinc and mercury — which element?
Cadmium: Chemical element with atomic number 48 (Cd)
Called the 'father of modern taxonomy,' which Swedish biologist formalized the two-name system for naming living things and was later ennobled as von Linné?
Carl Linnaeus: Swedish biologist and physician (1707–1778)
First flown in 1955 as a tricycle-gear evolution of an earlier taildragger model, this four-seat high-wing aircraft is the most-produced plane in history — which model is it?
Cessna 172: Propeller driven single engine aircraft.
Add this steely-grey transition metal (atomic number 24) to steel and you get stainless; polish it and it reflects nearly 70% of visible light without tarnishing. Which element is it?
Chromium: Chemical element with atomic number 24 (Cr)
Also known as ubiquinone, this antioxidant cofactor helps mitochondria produce ATP and gets its name from ten isoprenyl units in its molecular tail — what is it?
Coenzyme Q10: Biochemical cofactor and antioxidant. Coenzyme Q (CoQ), also known as ubiquinone, is a naturally occurring biochemical cofactor (coenzyme) and an antioxidant produced by the human body.
Found only in placental mammals, this roughly four-inch bundle of 200 to 300 million nerve fibers is the brain's largest white-matter structure, linking its left and right hemispheres — what is it?
Corpus callosum: White matter tract connecting the two cerebral hemispheres.
This herpesvirus genus's human species can cause mononucleosis in adults but birth defects affecting the eyes, ears, liver, and spleen when passed to a fetus — which virus?
Cytomegalovirus: Genus of viruses. The 11 species in this genus include Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV, HHV-5), which is the species that infects humans.
Marked by up to 20 liters of dilute urine a day and intense thirst that drinking barely satisfies, this condition comes in four types tied to problems with the hormone vasopressin — what is it?
Diabetes insipidus: Condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst.
Working alongside biochemist Katalin Karikó on nucleoside base modifications, this University of Pennsylvania immunologist shared the 2023 Nobel Prize for enabling COVID-19 mRNA vaccines — who is he?
Drew Weissman: American physician and immunologist (born 1959)
First described in 1821, this family of large herbivorous mammals features a snout modified into a trunk and includes extinct relatives such as mammoths — which taxonomic family?
Elephantidae: Family of mammals. The family was first described by John Edward Gray in 1821, and later assigned to taxonomic ranks within the order Proboscidea.

Arising in the food pipe that runs between the throat and the stomach, this disease's two main subtypes are a squamous-cell form common in the developing world and a glandular form more common in developed nations. What is it?
Esophageal cancer: Malignant neoplastic disease of the esophagus.
Carried out by the lungs, kidneys, and skin in vertebrates, this bodily process rids the body of metabolic byproducts like urea, carbon dioxide, and uric acid — what is it called?
Excretion: Elimination of metabolic waste products by an organism.

Sometimes nicknamed a 'cat' though it's actually the sole living member of its own genus in the weasel family, this North American forest mammal has been trapped for its fur since the 1700s — what is it?
Fisher (animal): Species of small, carnivorous mammal native to North America.

Unlike plants, this kingdom of life can't photosynthesize, and unlike most things, it has chitin in its cell walls — feeding instead by oozing digestive enzymes out and absorbing what dissolves. What group includes yeasts, molds, and mushrooms?
Fungus: Organism belonging to kingdom Fungi.
Endemic to China and sporting a handy 'thumb' on its forepaw to grip bamboo, this black-and-white bear weighs in around 100 to 115 kg — what animal is it?
Giant panda: Species of bear. The giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca), also known as the panda bear or simply panda, is a bear species endemic to China.
This large, widely distributed white wading bird nests in colonies built in trees near water and is now expanding its range into northern Europe — which species?
Great egret: Species of bird. The great egret (Ardea alba), also known as the common egret, large egret, great white egret, or great white heron, is a large, widely distributed egret.

Recognizable by V-shaped nostrils and a layer of blubber that keeps it warm in Arctic and temperate coastal waters, this pinniped is the most widely distributed of its kind and can weigh up to 370 pounds — which species?
Harbor seal: Species of pinniped. Blubber under the seal's skin helps to maintain body temperature.

Bred by Polynesians in the pre-Columbian era from two Pacific island species, this tropical flowering plant is the national flower of Malaysia and the unofficial national flower of Haiti — what is it?
Hibiscus × rosa-sinensis: Hybrid species of flowering plant. It is widely cultivated as an ornamental plant in the tropics and subtropics.
Carl Wilhelm Scheele pinned down this gas's composition in 1777; it's flammable, smells of rotten eggs, and kills by blocking cellular respiration much like cyanide — what colorless compound is it?
Hydrogen sulfide: Poisonous and flammable gas. Hydrogen sulfide (preferred IUPAC name and American English) or hydrogen sulphide (Commonwealth English) is a chemical compound with the formula H2S.
Patented in 1961 and used to fight fever, pain and inflammation by blocking the cyclooxygenase enzyme, this drug sits on the WHO's List of Essential Medicines — what is it?

His 1962 book The Calculus of Consent launched a theory of how politicians' and bureaucrats' self-interest shapes their decisions, earning him the 1986 Nobel in economics — which founder of public choice theory is this?
James M. Buchanan: American economist and Nobel Laureate (1919–2013)
Dubbed the 'Angel of Death,' this German physician held doctorates in both anthropology and medicine before joining the SS and selecting Auschwitz prisoners for the gas chambers — who was he?
Josef Mengele: Nazi SS doctor at Auschwitz (1911–1979)
Also called German turnip despite not being related to true turnips, this stout cabbage cultivar can be eaten raw or cooked, stem and leaves alike — what vegetable?
Kohlrabi: Biennial cultivar of wild cabbage.
Also known as Peruvian ginseng, this Andean root crop is grown at high altitude in Peru and Bolivia and exported worldwide as a dietary powder — what plant is it?
Lepidium meyenii: Plant species native to South America.
Developed under Kelly Johnson's Skunk Works team after the discovery of Germany's Me 262, this aircraft became the first jet fighter flown operationally by U.S. forces in World War II — which jet?
Lockheed P-80 Shooting Star: First jet aircraft in U.S. operational service.
Known historically as 'magnesia alba' to distinguish it from a manganese-containing mineral called 'magnesia nigra,' this white hygroscopic solid has the formula MgO — what is it?
Magnesium oxide: Chemical compound naturally occurring as periclase.
Widely brewed as a calming herbal tea despite limited clinical evidence for its effects, this annual plant in the daisy family goes by the nickname 'scented mayweed' — which plant?
Matricaria chamomilla: Species of flowering plant.
Marketed under brand names like Quaalude and Sopor, this sedative was pulled from commercial production in the mid-1980s due to widespread misuse — which drug?
Most under a millimeter long, these eight-legged arachnids include the parasite that plagues honeybee colonies and the species behind scabies in humans — what are they?
Considered a cultural universal present in every human society, this medium arranges sound into harmony, melody, and rhythm through composition, improvisation, and performance — what is it?
Music: Form of art using sound.

First arising in wormlike organisms 550 to 600 million years ago, this body-wide network splits into a central hub of brain and spinal cord and a peripheral web of nerve fibers relaying signals to and from every body part — which network?
Nervous system: Part of an animal that coordinates actions and senses.
This burrowing, semiaquatic South American rodent munches river-plant stems and was shipped worldwide by fur farmers, only to become a destructive invasive pest — which animal is it?
Nutria: Semi-aquatic rodent from South America.
In young children it can mean ear-pulling, extra crying, and poor sleep; it's a group of inflammatory diseases of the middle ear, from acute infections to lingering fluid. What's the medical name?
Otitis media: Inflammation of the middle ear. One of the two main types is acute otitis media (AOM), an infection of rapid onset that usually presents with ear pain.
Found in mice, cats, birds, humans, and dogs but absent in whales and most reptiles, this triangular bone is the body's largest sesamoid — what is it?
Patella: Kneecap, bone covering knee joint.
Known on the street as 'angel dust,' this dissociative anesthetic acts as an NMDA receptor antagonist and can cause hallucinations and psychosis — what is this drug?
Phencyclidine: Dissociative hallucinogenic drug, mostly used recreationally.

Commonly known as plantains or fleaworts — though unrelated to the banana-like cooking fruit of the same name — this genus of roughly 200 mostly herbaceous flowering plants tops out around 24 inches tall. Which genus?
Plantago: Genus of flowering plants. Plantago is a genus of about 200 species of flowering plants in the family Plantaginaceae, commonly called plantains or fleaworts.
This glucocorticoid medication used to suppress the immune system is actually a prodrug that the liver must convert into its active form before it works — what is it?
Prednisone: Steroid medication. It is also used to treat high blood calcium due to cancer and adrenal insufficiency along with other corticosteroids.
Often starting as a blood clot in the leg that travels to the lungs, this blockage can cause chest pain on breathing in, coughing up blood, and sudden death — what is the condition?

Pulmonary embolism: Blockage of an artery in the lungs. Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a blockage of an artery in the lungs by a substance that has moved from elsewhere in the body through the bloodstream (embolism).

Native to the eastern Himalayas and southwestern China, this small mammal sports dense reddish-brown fur, a ringed tail, and curved semi-retractile claws for climbing — and was the original bearer of its famous name. What is it?
Red panda: Species of mammal in Asia.
First created in 1994 near Darmstadt, Germany, this extremely radioactive synthetic element is named for the physicist who discovered X-rays — which element is it?
Roentgenium: Chemical element with atomic number 111 (Rg)
Also called elder or elderberry, this tree or shrub's flowers and berries are traditionally used to make cordial and wine — what's its scientific name?
Sambucus nigra: Species of flowering plant in the moschatel family.
When an infection-triggered immune overreaction sends blood pressure plummeting and disrupts cells throughout the body, doctors in the ICU are treating this life-threatening condition — what is it?
Septic shock: Dangerously low blood pressure due to damage from an organ infection.

Its last natural case appeared in 1977, and in 1980 the WHO declared it the only human disease ever wiped off the Earth — which scourge, known for fluid-filled blisters that scarred survivors, was it?
Commonly nicknamed phlegm, this mucus coughed up from the trachea and bronchi is examined for tell-tale yellow or green coloring that signals infection — what is it?
Sputum: Mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways.

Serving under both Presidents Sukarno and Suharto, this Indonesian economist held posts across trade, finance, and research ministries, and once lobbied Washington against Dutch colonial rule — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo: Indonesian statesman and economist (1917–2001)
Predicted by Mendeleev decades before its discovery and sitting in the periodic table between manganese and rhenium, what is the lightest element whose isotopes are all radioactive?
Technetium: Chemical element with atomic number 43 (Tc)
Native to the Mediterranean and a member of the mint family Lamiaceae, this dried herb's most common culinary variety, Thymus vulgaris, hails from Southeast Europe — what is it?
Thyme: Culinary herb. Thyme is a culinary herb consisting of the dried aerial parts of some members of the genus Thymus of flowering plants in the mint family Lamiaceae.
Its name translates to 'three-horned face,' and this frilled dinosaur roamed present-day western North America right up until the asteroid strike 66 million years ago — what dinosaur is it?
Triceratops: Genus of Late Cretaceous dinosaur.

Known by names like lingonberry and cowberry, this evergreen shrub's tart berries are a Nordic cuisine staple and are commercially grown in the Pacific Northwest and the Netherlands — what is its scientific name?
Vaccinium vitis-idaea: Species of shrub with edible fruit.
Tasteless, odorless, and nearly colorless, this polar molecule's strong hydrogen bonding makes it the solvent inside every known living organism — yet it offers no food energy at all. What is it?
Water: Chemical compound of hydrogen and oxygen.
This Greek economist served as Finance Minister under Alexis Tsipras during the 2015 debt crisis, becoming internationally known for battling EU-imposed austerity — who is he?
Yanis Varoufakis: Greek economist and politician (born 1961)
Mendelevium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for mendelevium is Md. Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Md and atomic number 101.
What is the chemical symbol for ytterbium?
The symbol for ytterbium is Yb. Ytterbium is a chemical element; it has symbol Yb and atomic number 70.

In what year was Sigourney Weaver born?
Sigourney Weaver: Susan Alexandra "Sigourney" Weaver ( sig-OR-nee; born October 8, 1949) is an American actress.
In what year was Michael Keaton born?
Michael Keaton: Michael John Douglas (born September 5, 1951), known professionally as Michael Keaton, is an American actor.
In what year was Eva Mendes born?
Eva Mendes: Eva de la Caridad Méndez (Spanish: [ˈeβa ðe la kaɾiˈðað ˈmendes]; born March 5, 1974), known professionally as Eva Mendes, is an American former actress.
In what year was Zooey Deschanel born?
Zooey Deschanel: Zooey Claire Deschanel (born January 17, 1980) is an American actress and singer.
In what year was David Tennant born?
David Tennant: David John Tennant (né McDonald; born 18 April 1971) is a Scottish actor.
In what year was Linda Cardellini born?
Linda Cardellini: Linda Edna Cardellini (born June 25, 1975) is an American actress.
In what year was Scott Adkins born?
Scott Adkins: Scott Edward Adkins (born 17 June 1976) is an English actor and martial artist.
In what year was Kevin Bacon born?
Kevin Bacon: Kevin Norwood Bacon (born July 8, 1958) is an American actor.
In what year was Song Kang born?
Song Kang (Korean: 송강; born April 23, 1994) is a South Korean actor.
In what year was Patrick Swayze born?
Patrick Swayze: Patrick Wayne Swayze ( SWAY-zee; August 18, 1952 – September 14, 2009) was an American actor, singer-songwriter and dancer.
In what year was Paul Reubens born?
Paul Reubens: Reubens developed his Pee-wee character at the Groundlings.
In what year did Truman Capote die?
Truman Capote: Capote had a troubled childhood caused by his parents' divorce, a long absence from his mother, and multiple moves.
In what year did Audrey Hepburn die?
Audrey Hepburn: Audrey Kathleen Hepburn (née Ruston; 4 May 1929 – 20 January 1993) was a British actress and humanitarian.
In what year was Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves first released?

Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves: 2023. The film received positive reviews from critics, with praise for the performances of the cast, the direction, visual effects, writing, score, humor, and tone.
In what year was Trainspotting first released?
